pr_title: Add new Task-based socket methods for UDP and reimplement existing ones using SocketAsyncEventArgs
pr_body:
Closes #41502, but does not change the existing APM methods, I plan to do it in a follow-up PR.

The PR is built on @geoffkizer's branch, almost all product code changes were written by him, I just added a bunch of tests, fixed an issue with Windows cancellation (4e4add1dabedfedd45a53e1060ecc13e2226220f), and moved extension methods to the `Socket` class as per #43901.

As such, the product code needs a third pair of yes to review. @stephentoub maybe?

Overall looks great, a couple thoughts above.

@geoffkizer just pushed a bunch of tests including ones for Dispose/Close/Shutdown/Disconnect cases, PTAL.

Intresting corner cases and platform differences I discovered while working on the tests:
1. Unlike `Close()`, `Shutdown()` does not seem to abort operations being already in flight
2. `shutdown()` works with UDP on Windows, but results in `ENOTCONN` on Linux
3. On Unix, `recvmsg()` works with ~UDP~ TCP sockets, while Windows `WSARecvMsg()` doesn't. From [docs](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/desktop/legacy/ms741687(v=vs.85)):
> The WSARecvMsg function can only be used with datagrams and raw sockets.

I wonder if any of the above is worth opening issues?

> Unlike Close(), Shutdown() does not seem to abort operations being already in flight

Interesting. Is that true on both Windows and Linux?

> shutdown() works with UDP on Windows, but results in ENOTCONN on Unix

That's odd, but I don't think it's a major concern. There's no real reason to do shutdown() with UDP. I suppose for consistency we should make Unix work like Windows, i.e. don't error (either eat the error or just skip the OS call entirely). Let's file an issue to consider, but I don't think it's a priority.

> On Unix, recvmsg() works with UDP sockets, while Windows WSARecvMsg() doesn't.

I'm confused... the did you mean TCP here?

Regardless, what's the implication of this in practice? Unix allows some TCP for ReceiveMessageFrom and Windows doesn't? Is ReceiveMessageFrom useful at all for TCP? Again, I suppose we should be consistent here but it's not a big deal.

> I'm confused... the did you mean TCP here?

yeah.

I don't think anyone uses `ReceiveMessageFrom` with TCP, I was just hunting for corner cases & compliance.
The code and tests all look good to me, but it looks like some of the Dispose tests are failing in CI. Do you know what's up here?

I see couple of things:
1. Either my `SendTo` (in-flight) cancellation tests are not robust enough, or cancellation does not work on some Unixes
2. `ShutdownReceiveBeforeOperation_ThrowsSocketException`: on some Windows environments doing `Shutdown(Both)` **before** `Receive(Message)From` doesn't lead to `WSAESHUTDOWN`. Weirdly, `Shutdown(Receive)` works. At this point I'm not sure if it's a sporadic or consistent thing.
3. There are couple of timeouts on Mac, weirdest is `AcceptGetsCanceledByDispose` (meaning we may have broken something)

Will continue investigating, looks like this stuff is more tricky than we expected.

issue_context.title: Sockets: Reimplement remaining Task-based async methods using SocketAsyncEventArgs
issue_context.body:
Most socket Task-based async APIs are implemented using SocketAsyncEventArgs under the covers today.

The few that are not include:

SendToAsync
ReceiveFromAsync
ReceiveMessageFromAsync

These are instead implemented by wrapping the old IAsyncResult-based async methods.

We should change these to use SocketAsyncEventArgs instead.

When doing so, we need to review the exceptions thrown by different implementations, and either decide to harmonize (-> break and document) or to keep compatibility. See: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/41585#issuecomment-683870587
@geoffkizer are you actually working on this? If not, I can give it a try.

I have a PR in progress for SendTo/ReceiveFrom/ReceiveMessageFrom. I haven't had time to look at it recently. If you'd like to take what I've got and finish it up, you are welcome to.

The other thing we should do here is to audit the code to see if there are any other methods besides this that are still using old IAsyncResult logic under the covers. I know the MultiConnect stuff was, but @stephentoub just fixed this. I think SendFile is another place -- see https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/42591.

There may be others as well, I'm not entirely sure...

> but @stephentoub just fixed this

Hasn't quite been merged yet, but will soon.
Just looked: DisconnectAsync doesn't have a Task-based version either (like SendFile). We need to add this.

FYI, that's called out in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/33417.  It had been its own issue at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/1608.

The other thing we should be looking at here is getting rid of the old IAsyncResult implementations and replacing them with wrappers on top of Task APIs. We should be able to do this for the APIs that already have Task implementations, i.e. Connect/Accept/Send/Receive. 

I thought there was an issue on this but I can't find it at the moment. Will add if necessary.
